Functions to filter data

The following code chunk creates the functions to filter data based on the user input. This is not used for the rest of this exercise, but will be utilised in the shiny app to pre-filter the dataset before perfoming the computations/displaying the graph.

  • Transaction type
  • Customer type
  • Transaction Date Range
filter_tx <- function(selected_type='All'){
 if(selected_type!='All'){
    result <- transactions %>%
      filter(type==selected_type)
    return(result)
 }
  else {
    return(transactions)
  }
}
filtered_tx <- filter_tx(selected_type="Payment")

filter_customer <- function(selected_type='All', selected_value='All'){
  if(selected_type!='All'){
      selected_cols <- customers %>%
          select(customer_id, all_of(selected_type), first_tx)
      if (!identical(selected_value, 'All')){
        filtered_customers <- selected_cols %>%
          filter(.data[[selected_type]] %in% selected_value)
      return(filtered_customers)
    } else {
      return(selected_cols)
    }
  }
  else{
    return(select(customers, customer_id, first_tx))
  }
}
filtered_cust <- filter_customer(selected_type='clv_segment',
                                 selected_value=c('Gold', 'Bronze', 'Silver'))

filter_tx_dates<- function(tx=transactions, start_date, end_date){
   result <- tx %>%
     filter(date>=ymd(start_date),
            date<=ymd(end_date))%>%
     mutate(week = yearweek(date),
            wk_date=as.Date(week))
   
   return(result)
}
filtered_tx_dates <- filter_tx_dates(transactions, "2023-01-01", "2023-3-30")

Seasonal Trend EDA

Filters

Filter Shiny widget type Values Function
Metric Radio buttons
  • Transaction Amount
  • Transaction Count
  • User Count
 Allow users to select what sort of transaction behaviour from customers they want to analyse

For

get_seasonal_data <- function(tx_df, cust_df, segmentation){
  result <- tx_df %>%
    inner_join(cust_df, by = "customer_id") %>%
    group_by(date, !!sym(segmentation)) %>%
    summarise(tx_count = n(),
            tx_amt = sum(amount),
            user_count = n_distinct(customer_id),
            .groups = 'drop') %>%
    as_tsibble(index = date, 
               key = !!sym(segmentation))
}
seasonal_data <- get_seasonal_data(filter_tx_dates(filtered_tx, 
                                                   '2023-01-01', 
                                                   '2023-12-31'), 
                                   filtered_cust, 
                                   "clv_segment")

seasonal_data %>%
  model(STLM=STL(tx_amt ~ season(period="1 month", window = 7) + trend(window = 14), robust = TRUE)) %>%
  components() %>%  
  autoplot() + 
  theme_grey() + 
  labs(
    title="STL decomposition - Payment Transactions"

Liquidity

Net Liquidity Visualisation

Data Preparation

First we will prepare the transaction data to represent inflows (deposits) and outflows (withdrawals). We take transfers as transfers made between accounts under the fintech company studied, hence we assume that the transfers do not affect the liquidity. Payments also not included

We will also create relevant columns to allow us to enhance the data visualisation later.

liquidity <- transactions %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, 
              values_from = amount,
              values_fn = sum) %>%
  replace_na(list(Withdrawal=0, Deposit=0)) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    Inflow=sum(Deposit),
    Outflow=sum(Withdrawal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = ifelse(Inflow > Outflow, "Inflow Higher", "Outflow Higher"),
         net_liquidity = Inflow-Outflow)

liquidity_wk <- transactions %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, 
              values_from = amount,
              values_fn = sum) %>%
  replace_na(list(Withdrawal=0, Deposit=0)) %>%
  mutate(week = yearweek(date),
         date=as.Date(week))%>%
  group_by(date, ) %>%
  summarise(
    Inflow=sum(Deposit),
    Outflow=sum(Withdrawal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = ifelse(Inflow > Outflow, "Inflow Higher", "Outflow Higher"),
         net_liquidity = Inflow-Outflow)
saveRDS(liquidity, "data/rds/liquidity.rds")
saveRDS(liquidity_wk, "data/rds/liquidity_wk.rds")
ggplot(liquidity_wk, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(Inflow, Outflow), 
                  ymax = pmax(Inflow, Outflow), 
                  fill = Group), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Inflow, color = "Inflow"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Outflow, color = "Outflow"), linewidth = 1) +
  # Styling
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Inflow" = "steelblue", "Outflow" = "coral")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Inflow Higher" = "steelblue", "Outflow Higher" = "coral")) +
  theme_grey() +
  labs(title = "Inflow vs. Outflow Over Time", 
       fill = "Net liquidity", color = "Series")

Forecasting

Split into training and test data

splits <- liquidity %>%
  initial_time_split(prop = 0.95)

Create models

model_fit_ets <- exp_smoothing() %>%
    set_engine(engine = "ets") %>%
    fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
        data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_arima <- arima_reg() %>%
  set_engine(engine = "auto_arima") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_arima_boosted <- arima_boost(
  min_n = 2,
  learn_rate = 0.015) %>%
  set_engine(
    engine = "auto_arima_xgboost") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_prophet <- prophet_reg() %>%
  set_engine(engine = "prophet") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
Disabling yearly seasonality. Run prophet with yearly.seasonality=TRUE to override this.
Disabling daily seasonality. Run prophet with daily.seasonality=TRUE to override this.
model_fit_prophet_boost <- prophet_boost() %>%
  set_engine("prophet_xgboost") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
Disabling yearly seasonality. Run prophet with yearly.seasonality=TRUE to override this.
Disabling daily seasonality. Run prophet with daily.seasonality=TRUE to override this.
model_fit_naive <- naive_reg() %>%
  set_engine("naive") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`),
      data = training(splits))
model_spec_glmnet <- linear_reg(
    mixture = 0.9,
    penalty = 4.36e-6
) %>%
    set_engine("glmnet")
models_tbl <- modeltime_table(
  model_fit_ets,
  model_fit_arima,
  model_fit_arima_boosted,
  model_fit_prophet,
  model_fit_prophet_boost,
  model_fit_naive
)

Calibrate model to testing set

calibration_tbl <- models_tbl %>%
    modeltime_calibrate(new_data = testing(splits), quiet=FALSE)
model_fit_ensemble <- calibration_tbl %>%
  modeltime.ensemble::ensemble_average(type = "mean")

# Add to your table
models_tbl <- models_tbl %>%
  add_modeltime_model(model_fit_ensemble)

Visualise and assess model accuracy on testing data

calibration_tbl %>%
  modeltime_accuracy %>%
  table_modeltime_accuracy()
